properties.natural_language: After ACTION-CHECK-FORK-BLOCK executes, the system MUST transition to STATE-PRE-FORK-MODE if block.number < FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER (13,773,000), or to STATE-POST-FORK-MODE if block.number >= FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-FAKE-BLOCK-NUMBER executes in post-fork mode, the computed fake_block_number MUST equal max(0, block.number - 10_700_000).
After ACTION-CALCULATE-DIFFICULTY completes, STATE-DIFFICULTY-CALCULATED MUST hold the expected difficulty value computed using the appropriate block number (actual for pre-fork, fake for post-fork).
The fake_block_number MUST never be negative; the max(0, ...) operation guarantees non-negativity for all block numbers.
The FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER constant (13,773,000) is immutable once consensus is activated; it MUST NOT change during runtime.
The approximate 7.5-month delay estimate assumes ~13.3 second average block times; implementations MUST NOT rely on calendar time for fork activation, only block number.
The difficulty bomb delay mechanism assumes network hashrate remains relatively stable; if hashrate drops significantly, bomb effects may manifest earlier than the ~10.7M block offset suggests.
The offset value 10,700,000 MUST be applied consistently to all difficulty calculations post-fork; partial application would create consensus divergence.
After ACTION-COMPARE-DIFFICULTY, the block MUST transition to STATE-BLOCK-DIFFICULTY-VALID if and only if the block stated difficulty exactly matches the computed expected difficulty.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-EXPECTED-DIFFICULTY, the expected difficulty MUST be computed using parent block data and the (possibly adjusted) block number per EIP-4345 rules.
A block in STATE-BLOCK-DIFFICULTY-INVALID MUST be rejected and never appended to the canonical chain.

After ACTION-PROCESS-FORK-BLOCK completes, the network MUST transition to STATE-NETWORK-POST-ARROW-GLACIER and subsequently to STATE-BOMB-DELAY-ACTIVE, applying the 10,700,000 offset to all future blocks.
The fork activation is irreversible: once STATE-NETWORK-POST-ARROW-GLACIER is reached, the system MUST NOT revert to STATE-NETWORK-PRE-ARROW-GLACIER.

Before processing any block from EDGE-PEER-BLOCK, the system MUST verify that the block header and body conform to expected format (extraData contains 32-byte vanity prefix and 65-byte ECDSA signature suffix).
At the EDGE-PEER-BLOCK boundary, block header fields MUST be validated for structural integrity before signer extraction: block number, parent hash, timestamp must be present and correctly formatted.
Locally produced blocks (EDGE-LOCAL-BLOCK) MUST undergo the same validation pipeline as peer-received blocks; local origin does not bypass any validation step.
After ACTION-EXTRACT-SIGNER, the recovered signer address MUST be a valid Ethereum address derived from the ECDSA signature in the last 65 bytes of extraData.
After ACTION-VERIFY-SIGNER-AUTHORIZED, the block MUST be rejected (STATE-SIGNER-UNAUTHORIZED) if the recovered signer is not in the current authorized signer set.
After ACTION-VERIFY-SIGNING-LIMIT, the block MUST be rejected (STATE-SIGNING-LIMIT-EXCEEDED) if the signer has signed more than 1 of the last floor(N/2)+1 consecutive blocks.
After ACTION-VERIFY-TIMESTAMP, the block MUST be rejected (STATE-TIMESTAMP-INVALID) if block.timestamp < parent.timestamp + BLOCK_PERIOD.
After ACTION-VERIFY-EXTRA-DATA and ACTION-VERIFY-CHECKPOINT complete successfully, the block transitions to STATE-BLOCK-VALID.
BLOCK_PERIOD is a network configuration parameter agreed upon at genesis; all nodes in the same Clique network MUST use the same BLOCK_PERIOD value for timestamp validation.
Checkpoint blocks MUST embed the complete ordered signer list in extraData, enabling light clients to verify subsequent blocks without full chain history.
Authorized signers are assumed to have reasonably synchronized clocks within BLOCK_PERIOD tolerance; clock skew exceeding this tolerance may cause valid block rejections.
Signer private keys are assumed securely stored; key compromise allows an attacker to produce valid blocks up to the signing frequency limit.
At EDGE-SIGNER-PROPOSES boundary, the vote (beneficiary + nonce) MUST originate from an authorized signer; votes from unauthorized addresses MUST be ignored.
At EDGE-SIGNER-PROPOSES boundary, the nonce value MUST be either 0xff...ff (AUTH vote) or 0x00...00 (DROP vote); any other value MUST be rejected.
After ACTION-CHECK-MAJORITY, transition to STATE-MAJORITY-AUTH requires AUTH votes >= floor(N/2)+1 from distinct authorized signers.
After ACTION-ADD-SIGNER or ACTION-REMOVE-SIGNER, ACTION-DISCARD-VOTES MUST clear all pending votes for the affected beneficiary before reaching STATE-SIGNER-SET-UPDATED.
After ACTION-RECORD-VOTE, the vote MUST be tallied via ACTION-TALLY-VOTES; each signer may cast only one active vote per beneficiary.
The authorized signer set MUST never become empty; the voting mechanism MUST prevent removal of the last signer.
Only one vote proposal is executed per block (the beneficiary of the current block); cascading execution of multiple simultaneous proposals is not permitted within a single block.

The Clique consensus model assumes a majority (>50%) of authorized signers are honest; if this assumption is violated, colluding signers can reorganize the chain and modify the signer set arbitrarily.
The system assumes attackers cannot sustain a network partition preventing honest signers from propagating blocks; partitioning could enable minority chain attacks.
After ACTION-CHECK-TURN, the signer MUST transition to STATE-SIGNER-IN-TURN if block_number % N == signer_index, otherwise to STATE-SIGNER-OUT-OF-TURN.
After ACTION-ASSEMBLE-BLOCK, the block difficulty MUST be set to 2 (INTURN) for in-turn signers or 1 (NOTURN) for out-of-turn signers.
After ACTION-SIGN-BLOCK, the ECDSA signature MUST be appended to extraData such that the signer address can be recovered from the signature over the header hash (excluding signature bytes).
After STATE-BLOCK-SIGNED, ACTION-BROADCAST-BLOCK MUST propagate the signed block to network peers.
After ACTION-ENFORCE-SIGNING-LIMIT against a malicious signer, STATE-SPAM-BLOCKED MUST be reached by rejecting blocks that exceed the 1-per-floor(N/2)+1 signing frequency.
After ACTION-EPOCH-VOTE-RESET, all votes older than one epoch MUST be discarded to prevent unbounded vote tracking growth.
After ACTION-VERIFY-51-PERCENT, STATE-MINORITY-CANNOT-TAKEOVER MUST be reached when the attacker controls fewer than floor(N/2)+1 signers.
After ACTION-VOTE-OUT-MALICIOUS with honest majority support, STATE-MALICIOUS-SIGNER-REMOVED MUST be reached, removing the compromised signer from the authorized set.

At EDGE-USER-DEPLOY-TX boundary, the deployer init code and constructor args are untrusted; the system MUST execute init code in a sandboxed EVM context and validate the resulting bytecode before storage.
At EDGE-USER-DEPLOY-TX boundary, the transaction MUST have a valid ECDSA signature and sufficient gas for init code execution; the deployer account is untrusted regarding code content.
After ACTION-CHECK-FIRST-BYTE, if the first byte of returned runtime bytecode equals 0xEF, the system MUST transition to STATE-FIRST-BYTE-IS-EF and subsequently trigger exceptional abort.
After ACTION-TRIGGER-EXCEPTIONAL-ABORT, STATE-DEPLOYMENT-ABORTED MUST be reached with all remaining gas consumed and no contract code stored.
After ACTION-EXECUTE-INIT-CODE completes, the returned runtime bytecode MUST be available for first-byte inspection before any storage occurs.
After ACTION-STORE-CONTRACT-CODE, STATE-CONTRACT-DEPLOYED MUST hold the validated runtime bytecode at the computed contract address in the account trie.
Empty bytecode (zero-length) returned from init code MUST be allowed; the 0xEF check only applies when code length >= 1.
Exceptional abort MUST behave identically to out-of-gas: all remaining gas consumed, no state changes persisted, operation fails.
Fork activation MUST be determined by accurate block number comparison against HF_BLOCK; incorrect fork detection could cause the 0xEF restriction to be applied or omitted incorrectly.
Pre-fork contracts starting with 0xEF are legitimate legacy code; the 0xEF restriction is NOT applied retroactively to existing deployed contracts.
No mechanism exists to deploy 0xEF-prefixed code without going through CREATE/CREATE2 validation; any bypass would compromise the EOF format reservation.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-CHILD-FIRST-BYTE, if child code starts with 0xEF, the system MUST abort the CREATE operation and push 0 to the parent stack.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-CHILD-FIRST-BYTE, if child code does NOT start with 0xEF, ACTION-DEPLOY-CHILD-CONTRACT MUST store code and push new address to parent stack.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-CREATE2-ADDRESS, the deterministic address MUST be computed from keccak256(0xff ++ sender ++ salt ++ keccak256(init_code)) before init code execution.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-CREATE2-FIRST-BYTE, if code starts with 0xEF, ACTION-ABORT-CREATE2 MUST consume gas and push 0 to stack; no contract at computed address.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-CREATE2-FIRST-BYTE with valid code, ACTION-DEPLOY-AT-ADDRESS MUST store code at the pre-computed deterministic address.
After ACTION-COMPARE-WITH-EF, the system MUST transition to STATE-BYTE-EQUALS-EF if byte == 0xEF, or STATE-BYTE-NOT-EF otherwise; this is a deterministic binary check.
STATE-BYTE-EQUALS-EF MUST always lead to STATE-VALIDATION-FAILED; STATE-BYTE-NOT-EF MUST always lead to STATE-VALIDATION-PASSED.
At EDGE-OPERATOR-PROVIDES-CHECKPOINT boundary, the weak subjectivity checkpoint MUST be validated for temporal validity (within weak subjectivity period) before use as sync bootstrap.
At EDGE-OPERATOR-PROVIDES-CHECKPOINT boundary, the checkpoint root MUST match a known valid state root; operator-provided checkpoints are semi-trusted but still require validation.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-WS-CHECKPOINT, the system MUST transition to STATE-CHECKPOINT-VALIDATED on success or STATE-CHECKPOINT-INVALID on failure; invalid checkpoints MUST NOT be used for sync.
After ACTION-SYNC-FROM-CHECKPOINT completes, STATE-CLIENT-SYNCED MUST hold with the client synchronized to the current chain head.
Node operators are trusted to provide valid weak subjectivity checkpoints; a malicious checkpoint could lead to syncing to an invalid chain state enabling long-range attacks.
At EDGE-PEER-PROVIDES-BLOCK boundary, block data from untrusted peers MUST be validated against consensus rules before storage; the pruning mechanism does not affect validation requirements.
At EDGE-PEER-PROVIDES-BLOCK boundary, block headers, bodies, and receipts MUST all be present and structurally valid before storage.
After ACTION-CHECK-DATA-AGE, data exceeding HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS (82,125 epochs / ~1 year) MUST transition to STATE-DATA-EXPIRED; data within the window returns to STATE-DATA-IN-RETENTION-WINDOW.
After ACTION-PRUNE-HISTORICAL-DATA, STATE-DATA-PRUNED MUST hold with headers, block bodies, and receipts removed from local storage.
After ACTION-STORE-BLOCK-DATA, block data MUST transition to STATE-DATA-IN-RETENTION-WINDOW where it is subject to periodic age checks.
HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS (82,125 epochs) MUST always exceed the weak subjectivity period to ensure checkpoint data remains available for new client synchronization.
At EDGE-PEER-REQUESTS-DATA boundary, the requesting peer is untrusted; the node MUST evaluate the request age before deciding to serve or decline, with no obligation to serve any data.
At EDGE-PEER-REQUESTS-DATA boundary, the block number range and request type MUST be validated for format correctness before age evaluation.
After ACTION-EVALUATE-REQUEST-AGE, requests for data within HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS transition to STATE-REQUEST-WITHIN-WINDOW; older requests transition to STATE-REQUEST-EXCEEDS-WINDOW.
After ACTION-SERVE-DATA, STATE-DATA-SERVED MUST hold with requested block data transmitted to peer. After ACTION-DECLINE-REQUEST, STATE-REQUEST-DECLINED MUST hold.
Clients SHOULD NOT serve historical data older than HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS; this is a soft requirement and clients MAY still serve old data but are not obligated.

At EDGE-EXTERNAL-RESPONSE boundary, historical data from untrusted external providers (IPFS, Portal Network, indexers) MUST be cryptographically verified against known state roots or accumulator proofs before acceptance.
At EDGE-EXTERNAL-RESPONSE boundary, historical blocks, receipts, and state proofs MUST each be individually validated; partial validation is insufficient.
At EDGE-DAPP-REQUESTS-HISTORY boundary, dApp requests for historical data MUST be treated as untrusted queries with no special privileges.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-EXTERNAL-DATA, data MUST transition to STATE-DATA-VALIDATED only if integrity verification against known state roots succeeds; otherwise STATE-DATA-INVALID.
Historical data validation from out-of-band sources MUST use accumulator proofs or state root verification; the specification gap in validation method is a critical security concern.
Out-of-band historical data sources (IPFS, Portal Network) are assumed to remain available; loss of all alternative data sources would make historical data permanently inaccessible.
Organizations are assumed to voluntarily maintain and distribute historical data; failure creates centralization risk with few entities controlling old data access.
External data providers (The Graph, indexing services) are assumed to serve authentic data; centralized providers could falsify historical data without detection if validation is not performed.
At EDGE-DAPP-REQUEST boundary, the chainId and optional parameters from the untrusted dApp MUST be validated for format (0x-prefixed EIP-155 compliant) before any processing.
At EDGE-DAPP-REQUEST boundary, the wallet MUST NOT automatically switch chains without explicit user confirmation; user consent is mandatory for all chain switches.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-CHAIN-ID, the system MUST branch to STATE-CHAIN-KNOWN if the wallet has existing configuration, or STATE-CHAIN-UNKNOWN if not.
After ACTION-PROMPT-USER-SWITCH or ACTION-PROMPT-USER-ADD, user decision MUST result in STATE-USER-APPROVED or STATE-USER-REJECTED; no default action without user input.
After STATE-USER-REJECTED, ACTION-RETURN-ERROR-4001 MUST return error code 4001 to the requesting dApp.
After ACTION-SWITCH-ACTIVE-CHAIN, STATE-WALLET-ON-CHAIN-B MUST hold with the wallet connected to the requested chain.
Chain switching changes the active chain for the current dApp session only; it MUST NOT modify the wallet persistent default chain configuration.
The security model assumes users can accurately evaluate chain switch legitimacy; users may be deceived by phishing leading to asset theft on malicious chains.
After ACTION-SANITIZE-URL fails, ACTION-REJECT-MALFORMED-URL MUST reject the request; URLs failing sanitization MUST NOT proceed to RPC verification.
After ACTION-CALL-ETH-CHAINID, STATE-RPC-VALID requires the returned chainId to match the requested chainId; mismatches transition to STATE-RPC-INVALID.
RPC URL sanitization MUST include: URL format validation, HTTPS protocol enforcement, blocking private/local IP ranges (127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x, 172.16-31.x), and URL injection attack prevention.
If provided RPC URLs fail validation, the entire chain switch request MUST be rejected with an appropriate error code.
The wallet is assumed to have access to a reliable default chain configuration list; without it, phishing attacks impersonating mainnet or popular chains may succeed without warning.
RPC validation requests (net_version, eth_chainId) are assumed not intercepted by MITM attacks; TLS/HTTPS enforcement mitigates this but is not specified in the EIP.
At EDGE-MALICIOUS-INPUT boundary, all chain switch parameters from attacker-controlled dApps MUST be treated as hostile: SSRF detection, chain list comparison, and user warnings MUST all apply.
At EDGE-MALICIOUS-INPUT boundary, RPC URLs MUST be analyzed for internal resource targeting (localhost, private IPs) before any network request is made.
After ACTION-DETECT-SSRF-ATTEMPT finds internal targets, STATE-SSRF-BLOCKED MUST be reached and the request blocked (STATE-REQUEST-BLOCKED).
After ACTION-CHECK-DEFAULT-CHAIN-LIST detects chain name mismatches, STATE-PHISHING-DETECTED MUST trigger ACTION-WARN-USER to alert about the risk.

After ACTION-COMPUTE-CRC32, FORK_HASH MUST be the IEEE CRC32 checksum computed over the genesis hash concatenated with all past fork block numbers encoded as uint64 big-endian, with duplicates removed.
After ACTION-DETERMINE-NEXT-FORK, STATE-FORK-ID-READY MUST hold with FORK_NEXT set to the next known fork block number, or 0 if no fork is scheduled.
Duplicate fork block numbers (multiple EIPs at same block) MUST be checksummed only once; each unique block number appears once in the CRC32 input.
CRC32 collision probability is assumed sufficiently low for practical use; different configurations producing the same FORK_HASH would allow incompatible peer connections.
Nodes are assumed to have accurate knowledge of past and upcoming fork block numbers; incorrect configuration produces wrong FORK_HASH causing network rejection.
At the peer fork ID reception boundary, the remote fork ID is self-reported without cryptographic proof; the validation rules MUST be applied defensively assuming the remote could be lying.
Before comparing fork hashes, both local and remote fork ID values MUST be available and properly formatted (4-byte FORK_HASH, uint64 FORK_NEXT).
After ACTION-COMPARE-FORK-HASH, matching hashes lead to ACTION-CHECK-HEAD-POSITION; differing hashes lead to ACTION-CHECK-SUBSET-SUPERSET.
After ACTION-CHECK-HEAD-POSITION with matching hashes, peer MUST be accepted if remote FORK_NEXT has not yet passed locally; rejected if it has.
After ACTION-CHECK-SUBSET-SUPERSET with differing hashes, peer MUST be accepted if valid subset/superset relationship exists (syncing scenario); rejected if incompatible.
Remote superset relationship means the remote FORK_HASH can be reproduced by adding known upcoming forks to the local chain configuration.
When fork schedules change (postponed/cancelled), FORK_NEXT MUST be updated and peer fork IDs recalculated accordingly.
Peers are assumed to report fork IDs honestly; malicious peers lying about fork IDs waste connection resources and could prevent legitimate syncing.
After ACTION-ENCODE-FORK-ID, the fork ID MUST be RLP-encoded as [FORK_HASH, FORK_NEXT] for inclusion in the ENR.
After ACTION-EXTRACT-FORK-ID from a discovered peer ENR, ACTION-PRE-FILTER-PEER MUST check compatibility before attempting a full connection.
After all module loading actions complete in sequence (state, transactions, blocks, VM), STATE-MODULES-READY MUST hold with all Cancun fork components initialized.
Module loading order is assumed to be flexible with no circular dependencies; modules can be initialized in any order without deadlock.
All required cryptographic libraries and dependencies MUST be available in the execution environment; missing dependencies would cause fork activation failure.
The fork.py module is assumed to correctly implement all Cancun consensus rule changes; incorrect implementation causes consensus split.
After ACTION-RAISE-EXCEPTION, STATE-EXCEPTION-RAISED MUST be reached and ACTION-HANDLE-EXCEPTION MUST process the error, resulting in STATE-OPERATION-FAILED with state rollback.
When STATE-OPERATION-FAILED is reached, all state changes from the failed operation MUST be rolled back; no partial state mutations may persist.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-TRIE-ROOT, STATE-TRIE-ROOT-COMPUTED MUST hold the Merkle Patricia Trie root hash that cryptographically commits to all input data.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-BLOOM, STATE-BLOOM-COMPUTED MUST hold a 2048-byte bloom filter suitable for efficient log topic lookup.
After ACTION-HASH-COMMITMENT, the SHA256 hash of the 48-byte KZG commitment MUST be computed correctly before version byte prepending.
After ACTION-PREPEND-VERSION, STATE-VERSIONED-HASH-READY MUST hold a 32-byte value with 0x01 as first byte followed by 31 bytes of the truncated SHA256 hash.
Versioned hash format MUST be: 1 byte version (0x01) + 31 bytes of SHA256 hash = 32 bytes total; the truncation length is 31 bytes.
At EDGE-RECEIVE-BYTES48 boundary, untrusted 48-byte input MUST be validated as a valid G1 point or point at infinity before use in cryptographic operations.
At EDGE-RECEIVE-BYTES48 boundary, the input MUST be exactly 48 bytes; length validation MUST occur before G1 point parsing.
At EDGE-RECEIVE-BYTES32 boundary, untrusted 32-byte input MUST be validated against the BLS modulus before conversion to a field element.
After ACTION-CHECK-INFINITY, the G1 point at infinity (0xc0 + 47 zero bytes) MUST be accepted as valid without further BLS verification.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-G1-POINT, the system MUST transition to STATE-G1-POINT-VALID on successful BLS verification, or STATE-G1-POINT-INVALID on failure.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLS-MODULUS, input MUST be accepted (STATE-FIELD-ELEMENT-VALID) if value < BLS modulus, or rejected (STATE-FIELD-ELEMENT-INVALID) otherwise.
G1 point validation failure MUST raise an exception that propagates to the caller, rejecting the entire operation; silent failures are not permitted.
At EDGE-RECEIVE-PROOF-INPUTS boundary, all four inputs (commitment 48B, z 32B, y 32B, proof 48B) MUST have their byte lengths validated before any cryptographic processing.
At EDGE-RECEIVE-PROOF-INPUTS boundary, proof verification inputs from untrusted sources MUST undergo type conversion validation (G1 point, field element checks) before pairing operations.
After ACTION-CONVERT-TO-CRYPTO-TYPES completes, STATE-CRYPTO-TYPES-READY MUST hold with all inputs validated and converted to KZGCommitment, BLSFieldElement, and KZGProof types.
After ACTION-PAIRING-CHECK, STATE-PROOF-VALID MUST hold if and only if the pairing equals FQ12.one(); otherwise STATE-PROOF-INVALID.
The trusted setup parameter KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL_1 is assumed correctly generated and not compromised; compromise would allow forging proofs for arbitrary data.
Attacker cannot efficiently compute discrete logarithms in BLS12-381 groups; this assumption underpins all KZG proof security.
BLS12-381 pairing operations are assumed correctly implemented in underlying library; bugs could cause valid proofs to be rejected or invalid proofs accepted.
After ACTION-UPDATE-BLOCKCHAIN-HEIGHT processes a new block, STATE-METRICS-UPDATED MUST hold the ethereum_blockchain_height gauge reflecting the latest processed block number.
After ACTION-UPDATE-BEST-KNOWN-BLOCK during sync, the ethereum_best_known_block_number MUST reflect the highest block reported by peers or current height when synced.
After ACTION-UPDATE-PEER-COUNT, the ethereum_peer_count metric MUST accurately reflect the current number of connected peers.
After STATE-SYNCING reaches sync target, STATE-SYNC-COMPLETE MUST hold with the client fully synchronized.
At EDGE-SCRAPE boundary, metrics scrape requests from Prometheus MUST be validated for authorization; the endpoint SHOULD only be accessible to trusted monitoring systems.
At EDGE-SCRAPE boundary, the metrics endpoint MUST NOT expose sensitive information (private keys, internal state) that could enable attacks if accessed by unauthorized parties.
After ACTION-FORMAT-PROMETHEUS, STATE-RESPONSE-SENT MUST contain metrics in valid Prometheus exposition format.
The metrics endpoint path and port are not specified in the EIP; implementations MUST use standard Prometheus conventions (/metrics path) on a configurable port.
ethereum_best_known_block_number MUST be derived from peer announcements during sync or current height when synced; the estimation method must be consistent across implementations.
Additional client-specific metrics SHOULD use client-specific prefixes (e.g., geth_, besu_) to avoid namespace conflicts with ethereum_ standard metrics.
The metrics endpoint is assumed accessible only to authorized monitoring systems; unauthorized access reveals operational intelligence about sync state, peer count, and block height.
All client implementations are assumed to interpret metric definitions identically; inconsistent interpretation causes misleading cross-client monitoring dashboards.
The Prometheus server is assumed to be a trusted monitoring system; malicious actors with metrics access could time attacks based on sync state or peer count.
After ACTION-CHECK-PREFIX, metrics with ethereum_ prefix MUST be validated against standard definitions; non-prefixed metrics are client-specific and unconstrained.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-STANDARD-DEFINITION, STATE-STANDARD-METRIC indicates correct standard metric; STATE-INVALID-METRIC indicates unauthorized use of ethereum_ prefix.
At EDGE-DESERIALIZE-INPUT boundary, SSZ bytes from untrusted data sources MUST be structurally validated (length, format) before deserialization; malformed input MUST be rejected.
At EDGE-DESERIALIZE-INPUT boundary, the active_fields bitvector within serialized data MUST be extracted and validated before field deserialization begins.
After ACTION-SERIALIZE-CONTAINER, STATE-CONTAINER-SERIALIZED MUST hold a compact byte representation where absent fields consume no space.
After ACTION-DEFAULT-ABSENT-FIELDS, STATE-CONTAINER-DESERIALIZED MUST hold the reconstructed container with absent fields zero-initialized to their default values.
After ACTION-MERKLEIZE-PROGRESSIVE, STATE-MERKLE-TREE-COMPUTED MUST hold a Merkle tree where each field occupies a stable generalized index regardless of active_fields configuration.
After ACTION-MIX-IN-ACTIVE-FIELDS, STATE-HASH-TREE-ROOT-COMPUTED MUST include the active_fields hash mixed into the Merkle root, preventing collision between absent-field and zero-value containers.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-NON-EMPTY, containers with zero fields MUST transition to STATE-EMPTY-CONTAINER-ERROR; non-empty containers proceed to max fields validation.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-MAX-FIELDS, containers with more than 256 active fields MUST transition to STATE-MAX-FIELDS-ERROR.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-NO-TRAILING-ZEROS, active_fields ending with 0 MUST transition to STATE-TRAILING-ZERO-ERROR.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-FIELD-COUNT-MATCH, STATE-SCHEMA-VALID is reached only when all four validations pass; STATE-FIELD-COUNT-MISMATCH-ERROR on count mismatch.
EIP-7916 defines the underlying progressive Merkle tree; EIP-7495 builds container semantics on top. Implementation order must respect this dependency.
256 bits is a hard protocol limit for active_fields; containers requiring more fields need a different mechanism.
At EDGE-RECEIVE-PROOF boundary, Merkle proofs from untrusted sources (light clients, smart contracts) MUST be cryptographically verified against the expected root before accepting any field values.
At EDGE-RECEIVE-PROOF boundary, the proof and field value MUST be structurally validated before generalized index computation begins.
After ACTION-VERIFY-PROOF-PATH, if path verification fails, STATE-PROOF-INVALID MUST be reached immediately; successful path verification proceeds to active_fields mix-in check.
After ACTION-VERIFY-ACTIVE-FIELDS-MIXIN, STATE-NO-COLLISION-GUARANTEED MUST confirm that the active_fields mix-in prevents hash collision between absent fields and zero-valued fields.
Verifiers trust that active_fields accurately represents which fields are present; forged active_fields could create colliding hashes for different container configurations.
Light clients and smart contracts are assumed to have access to correct container schema definitions; outdated schemas cause proof misinterpretation.
The hash function used for Merkleization (SHA256) is assumed collision-resistant; collisions would allow forging Merkle proofs for arbitrary field values.
Attackers are assumed unable to manipulate serialized representations to create valid-looking containers with forged field values; structural validation prevents this.
